name: NOCIL Ltd
title: NOCIL Ltd - 500730 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: NOCIL Q4 FY26 revenue rose 5% QoQ to Rs.330 crore on 7% volume growth, but EBITDA margin fell to 6.4% amid raw material inflation.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was Rs.330 crore, up 5% QoQ from Rs.316 crore, with volumes up 7% QoQ, driven by domestic demand after GST 2.0 and steady single-digit international growth. Operating EBITDA fell to Rs.21 crore (6.4% margin) from Rs.27 crore in Q3, hit by gas-driven utility costs, shutdown maintenance and a Rs.7-8 crore inventory-related stock change debit. FY26 revenue fell to Rs.1,303 crore from Rs.1,393 crore, with full-year volumes up 3% and PAT down to Rs.56 crore from Rs.103 crore. Management raised prices on non-contractual business in March and on contractual business from Q1 FY27 in response to sharp raw material inflation linked to Middle East disruption.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic volumes grew single digits QoQ, aided by GST 2.0 demand; management estimates a 100-150 bps market share gain. Volume split FY26 is 70% domestic, 30% exports.

segments.name: International / Exports
segments.commentary: International volumes grew steady single digits in Q4. Export value share is about 33% (67:33 domestic:export by value). US volumes, hit roughly 50% last quarter by duties, are recovering but management expects traction only in FY27.

segments.name: Specialty rubber chemicals
segments.commentary: Specialty is about 15% of mix today, with management targeting about 20% after the new Rs.130 crore integrated specialty facility ramps up.

guidance_outlook: Management expects H2 FY26 volume momentum (up 12% YoY) to continue into coming quarters, and says Q4 volumes can serve as the base run rate.
Targets double-digit volume growth in coming years.
Targets EBITDA improvement of about 150 bps from the FY26 base going forward.
Price increases on non-contractual business taken in March and on contractual business from Q1 FY27; management sees the current raw material spike as volatility, not structural demand weakness.
Expects 6-8 months from commissioning before material traction from tyre-based customers on new capacity; non-tyre business should start earlier.
Tax rate reverts to normal rates in FY27 with no specific reduction expected.
capex_capacity: TDQ capex at Dahej (announced 26 March 2024) is complete; trial production has started and samples go to customers for approval. Total capex is under Rs.250 crore.

New Rs.130 crore capex announced 16 March 2026 for a comprehensive integrated specialty rubber chemicals facility at Dahej, expected complete by H1 FY28. Mostly growth capex with some intermediates; largely merchant per management, with a part captive.
Installed capacity cited by analysts at about 1,38,000-1,39,000 tons; management declined to give effective capacity, saying utilisation is roughly 65%.
CWIP was about Rs.220 crore at FY26 end; no project debt drawn yet, with bank lines above Rs.100 crore available at repo-linked rates.
Full-year FY26 capex was largely funded from internal working capital release; analysts estimated Rs.170-180 crore working capital saving.
demand_pricing: Realisations were under pressure from low-priced imports through Q4; management says the market corrected finished goods prices after April input price rises.
About 65-70% of volume is under contract, with the rest non-contractual; roughly 40% of revenue is exposed to anti-dumping products.

DGTR gave positive final findings in March 2026 for antioxidant TDQ and Sulphenamides (CBS and NS), subject to central government approval, which management expects around mid-June (about 90 days). Pilflex 13 and 4ADPA findings are pending, with Pilflex 13 expected within a month or two.
Imports rose in Jan-Feb 2026 YoY; management linked this to FTA routes (Thailand, Korea) and year-end advance-licence imports. The company is pressing the government on FTA value-addition norms.
Management assumes 2-2.5% long-term global rubber demand growth, and 7% domestic demand growth per ICRA.
Competitive intensity is rising from Chinese players in latex, and 6PPD alternatives are at trial stage, with the company working on them.

qa_highlights.question: Are customers negotiating on price or prioritising volume security, and what is the contract mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says talks are positive but weighted to supply reliability; contract share is about 65-70%, with the rest non-contract and repriced first.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA not benefit from inflation given inventory on hand?
qa_highlights.answer: Legacy high-cost inventory from the prior year spilled into H1 FY26, and the FTA-driven removal of basic duty on one product compressed spreads. Q4 also had a Rs.7-8 crore stock change debit and March production cuts from gas costs.

qa_highlights.question: Will ADD on TDQ and Sulphenamides lift margins, and what are the timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quantum is premature to assess; the Finance Ministry decision is expected around mid-June, and historically exporters have absorbed duties, so net benefit is uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume and mix outlook for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets double-digit volume growth in coming years, with new products adding to volumes gradually through FY27 and not yet material.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rs.130 crore project's volume impact and is it merchant?
qa_highlights.answer: Largely additional capacity, not debottlenecking; the Rs.250 crore Dahej capex volume is fully merchant. The Rs.130 crore project is partly captive intermediates. Capacity figures were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company still confident about cost reduction and conversion cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilities and other expenses fell by about Rs.10-11 crore; other expenses fell Rs.18-20 crore in FY26. No specific FY27 conversion-cost target was given.

risks_watch: Raw material supply (amines, MIBK) and gas-linked costs amid Middle East disruption; management says supplies are secure for the next few weeks.
Outcome of central government review of ADD on TDQ and Sulphenamides (around mid-June), and pending Pilflex 13 and 4ADPA DGTR findings.
Whether price hikes actually stick in Q1 FY27 given import competition and customer volume-security concerns.
Margin trajectory: EBITDA margin fell to 6.4% in Q4 and 7.7% for FY26, versus 13-15% cited at Dahej capex announcement.
Ramp-up timing of new Dahej capacity, with tyre-customer approvals taking 6-8 months.
Environmental regulation risk on 6PPD, the largest rubber chemical, with alternatives still in trial.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume momentum and long-term growth, but cautious on margins. Management called the Q4 margin dip partly one-off and attributed it to gas costs and inventory effects. Evasive on ADD quantum, price-hike size and capacity figures, citing business sensitivity.
key_quotes: So we are quite positive that we will be able to build on this into the next quarter.
At this stage, we see this more as a volatility and cost management challenge rather than a structural demand issue.
So we are looking at double-digit growth in terms of volumes, that's the target for the coming years.
